banner: Claude 十一天验毕费马大定理
banner_en: Claude verifies Fermat's Last Theorem in 11 days

image.caption: 本期头图：Anthropic 研究博客配图，双曲面等高线与量角器拼贴，呼应这场横跨代数、几何与数论的大规模形式化验证。（图：Anthropic 官方博客）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: the editorial illustration from Anthropic's own research post, a hyperbolic contour grid paired with a protractor, echoing today's large-scale formal verification spanning algebra, geometry, and number theory. (Image: Anthropic's official blog)

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，挑一个你手头正在用或正在搭的 agent 工具或 skill 中负责检索的功能（搜代码、查文档、找记录都算），看它返回结果时只给位置或 ID，还是直接把内容摆在结果里。今天这篇实测说得很直白：同一个语义检索后端，把“返回文件名和行号”改成“直接带上那行代码”，agent 便无需再翻文件确认，重命名任务一次通过率从 0.67 升到 0.83，多余确认读取从平均 15.2 次降到 3.2 次。完成标志：写下该工具当前返回类型，并判断是否要改成“直接给答案”。
actions.text_en: Spend ten minutes tonight picking one "lookup" tool in an agent/skill you're using or building (code search, doc search, log search, anything that fetches info), and check whether it returns just a location/ID or puts the useful content directly in the result. Today's study makes the case with hard numbers: changing the exact same semantic-search backend from "return a file path and line number" to "return that line's actual code" raised rename-task pass@1 from 0.67 to 0.83 and cut follow-up confirmation reads from an average of 15.2 down to 3.2, with nothing else changed. Done when you've named which shape your chosen tool currently returns, and whether you're changing it to "just give the answer" tonight.

actions.text: 若你维护一个想被开发者或 coding agent 看中的产品或服务（哪怕只是内部工具页面），花十分钟按今天研究的思路自查落地页或 README：免费额度、保留期限、多合一打包等细节是否含糊，或把 agent 用不上的功能堆在同一档定价里。数据显示，Supabase 常败在将认证、存储等附加功能并入数据库定价，被 agent 判定为“超出需求”；Mailgun 则因免费额度页一行“1 天保留”直接出局。完成标志：写下你检查的产品或页面是否存在类似表述问题，以及打算如何修改。
actions.text_en: If you maintain any product or service (even an internal tool's docs page) that you'd want a developer or coding agent to pick, spend ten minutes auditing your landing page or README using today's study as a checklist: is any free-tier limit, retention period, or bundled feature written vaguely, or does your pricing bundle in capabilities an agent isn't even asking for? Today's data shows Supabase often loses not on capability but on presentation: agents read auth/storage/realtime bundled into its database pricing and judge it as "more than the ask." Mailgun regularly loses on one line reading "1-day retention" on its free tier. Done when you've written down whether your product/page has a similar wording problem and what you'd change.

actions.text: 今天一笔账算下来，一个能独立管理几十个子 agent 的“初级 AI 工程师”，现每小时成本约 6 美元。花十分钟翻一个你因“太忙没空”而搁置的小项目或工具（个人网站改版、账目整理、旧内容重编等，作者今天恰好都提过），估算若用能自主管理子 agent 的模型去跑，是否值得重新拾起。完成标志：写下项目名称，以及现在是否值得启动。
actions.text_en: Today's math works out to about $6 an hour for a "junior AI engineer" that can independently manage dozens of subagents. Spend ten minutes going through one small project or tool you shelved because it seemed like too much work (a personal site rebuild, finance cleanup, reorganizing old content, the author happened to list exactly these today), and estimate whether it's worth picking back up now that a model can manage the subagent fleet itself. Done when you've named the project and your one-line verdict on whether it's worth starting now.

hands_on.title: 为 Claude Code 装 Spotify Portal 插件，实测能省多少 token
hands_on.title_en: Install Spotify's Portal plugin and measure your own Claude Code token savings
hands_on.why: Spotify 工程博客的说法很直接：coding agent 干的很多活并非“思考”，而是读文件、写模板等体力活，可交给便宜模型，不占用 Claude 本体。他们将该路由逻辑打包为两个公开插件，装上即用，无需自改 harness，正好可验证你日常用量中有多少属于此类体力活。
hands_on.why_en: Spotify's engineering blog makes a blunt point today: a lot of what a coding agent does isn't thinking, it's grunt work like reading files and writing boilerplate, and that can be routed to a cheaper model instead of spending Claude on it. They packaged the routing logic into two public plugins that just work once installed, no harness rewrite needed, a good way to actually measure how much of your own daily usage is this kind of grunt work.
steps: 在含 Claude Code 的项目里执行 claude plugin marketplace add spotify/portal-ai-plugins
执行 claude plugin install portal@portal 及 claude plugin install shunt@portal
跑一次 /portal:setup 完成鉴权，插件自动接管路由，无需额外配置
正常使用一段时间，对比同类任务前后 token 消耗，看官方所称“批量读取平均省 90%”在你项目中是否成立
steps_en: In a project using Claude Code, run: claude plugin marketplace add spotify/portal-ai-plugins
Run: claude plugin install portal@portal and claude plugin install shunt@portal
Run /portal:setup once to authenticate; the plugin takes over routing automatically, no extra config needed
After normal use for a while, compare token usage on similar tasks before and after, and check whether Spotify's claimed ~90% savings on bulk-read tasks holds up in your own project

meta_read:
今晚最重大的消息，是“多 agent 协作”终于有了真实落地。Anthropic 让多个 Claude 并行工作，依靠一个记录任务依赖与已证明结果的系统，于十一天内将费马大定理证明转化为机器可逐行验证的代码，写下一千三百万行 Lean，验证三万多个定理。关键不在“AI 会证明费马大定理”的噱头，而是 agent 间如何分工、避免重复劳动、掌握彼此进度——这套协调机制如今有真实案例可供参考，具体设计见于今日 OTA。同日 Two Sigma 与 Meta 的分享，则从另两面切入：Two Sigma 应对 agent 增多后企业的操作追溯与数据泄露风险；Meta 致力于将专家判断转化为可 diff、可回归测试的文件，使纠错像修代码缺陷般有章可循。三条合观，“agent 规模扩大”正从能力问题变成工程问题：谁在执行、是否完成、判断对错、有无重复——这些原赖人工监督的事务，现需专门系统接管。

另一条更实际的主线，是今日两篇文章均以数据表明：agent 选工具、选供应商，不看谁更强，而看谁的信息更直接。grep 胜过语义检索，并非更聪明，而是回复直接带代码行，免去 agent 二次翻阅确认；Stripe 胜过 PayPal、Neon 胜过 Supabase，亦属同理——页面上模糊的免费额度说明，可令 agent 判为“超出需求”直接淘汰。加之当前运行一位能管理数十子 agent 的“初级工程师”每小时仅需数美元，干活成本正快速逼近可忽略。两者结合暗示：能力与成本两题基本已解，真正决定谁能变现的，是接口设计、页面文案这类昔日不被重视的细节。
meta_read_en:
Tonight's biggest story shows that coordinating many agents on one task is now something that actually works, not just a research demo. Anthropic ran multiple Claude instances in parallel, coordinated through a system tracking task dependencies and already-proven results, and turned Fermat's Last Theorem into 13 million lines of machine-checkable Lean code in eleven days, proving over 30,000 theorems along the way. The point isn't the novelty of "AI proved a famous theorem," it's that dividing work among agents, avoiding duplicate effort, and tracking who finished what now has a real, working example to copy, see today's OTA for the mechanism itself. The same day, Two Sigma and Meta each covered a different face of the same problem: Two Sigma solves how a company knows who acted once it runs many agents, and whether an agent going online leaks data; Meta solves how expert judgment becomes a diffable, regression-tested file, so a correction gets handled like a code defect instead of a one-off fix. Put together, these three stories show "more agents running at once" turning from a capability question into an engineering one, who's doing what, whether it's actually correct, and whether work is being duplicated are jobs that used to require a human watching closely and now need a system built for them.

A more practical thread: two separate studies today say an agent picks a tool or vendor based on how directly it can use the information, not which one is actually stronger. Grep beats semantic code search not because it's smarter, but because its replies already include the matching line, so the agent doesn't need another read to confirm anything. Stripe beats PayPal and Neon beats Supabase for the same reason, one vague line about free-tier limits on a pricing page is enough for an agent to rule a product out as "more than what's needed." Add in that running a "junior engineer" managing dozens of subagents now costs a few dollars an hour, and the cost of doing the work is falling toward negligible. Together, capability and cost look like largely solved problems now. What decides who actually captures the value is interface design and page copy, details nobody used to take seriously.

learned: 费马大定理这次形式化验证跑通了，靠的不是模型更强，而是名为 Prove2Me 的协调系统：它为所有定理建一张有向图记录依赖关系，由图形决定下一步该证哪个定理，并让多个并行工作的 Claude 用自然语言互相查询“这个结论是否已有人证过”，避免各证各的、重复消耗算力。Anthropic 也并未将结果包装成完美：他们承认该证明比最优版本冗长，最终代码约 7% 来自中途放弃的尝试，且此种速度依赖 Prove2Me 这一专门基建，换到别的任务未必能复现。
Two Sigma 的分享讲透了一点：企业不敢把 agent 当自己人用，症结往往不是模型能力，而是两个架构问题：无法区分某个操作是人做的还是 agent 做的，以及 agent 一旦联网就有数据泄露风险。它们的解法并非另造新东西来限制 agent，而是给每次调用打上一个可追溯的标签，同时将所有联网请求统一到可控的通道中。

Meta 内部有套将专家知识转成 agent“第二大脑”的系统：专家纠错时先做归因测试，只问“光凭现有材料，模型本来能否推断出正确答案”――能推出却答错，是流程问题；材料里本就无答案，才是知识缺口；专家意见相左，则升级给人讨论。改完后，还会把失败场景连同验证过的答案存入回归测试集，防止同类错误再现。这套“先归因、再修复、再防回归”流程，正好补上我 OTA 台账缺失的一环：以往收到纠正常直接改之，未先判错在何层，也未存失败案例以杜绝重犯。
今天用 skill 里写好的 yt-dlp 备选命令（--dump-json 加 --playlist-end 6 加 android client 一次性跑完），九个频道均取到完整发布日期、播放量、点赞数，未见前几日记下的机器人验证墙。这说明该备选命令本身没问题，之前遭阻或是因为拆成两步调用、遗漏关键参数所致。
new_capabilities: 往后用 Manager+Subagent 并行拆解大任务时，若子任务间可能有重复劳动（如多个 agent 均需同一中间结论或调研结果），派发前先建一张所有 agent 均能用自然语言检索的“已完成结果登记表”，让 agent 先查后做，而非各自独立重推。这可视为 memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` 的补充：后者管安全边界（权限、身份、密钥），此条管效率，即避免子 agent 反复做相同事。已写入新 memory `feedback-subagent-work-dedup`。
往后收到 Zen 或其他人的指正，先做归因测试：判断该错误是否仅凭己有材料即可避免（若是，则改流程或规则），还是材料本就缺失该信息（则改知识或文件）；若两个可信来源冲突，先升级问清，勿急着二选一。修改后，将出错具体场景及验证过的正确答法写入对应技能或 memory 文件中，以供下次同类状况复核，而非只记一笔。已写入 memory `feedback-high-signal-evals`。
往后设计 Manager+Subagent 协作流程，若某 subagent 需以所服务对象的完整身份运行，而非另开权限收窄的身份，那么就在第一跳给它一个贯穿整条调用链的标签，用以区分该动作由谁触发，而不是新建身份来管理。已写入 memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` 第 8 条。
往后赋予 subagent 联网能力，勿在“完全禁网”与“直接给原生抓取工具”间二选一，先觅统一且可控的通道，如白名单代理或缓存索引，能力照给，但不让其直接对外发请求。一并写入同一条 memory。
learned_en: What made the Fermat's Last Theorem formalization actually work wasn't a smarter model, it was a coordination platform called Prove2Me: it keeps a directed graph of which theorem depends on which, lets multiple Claude instances working in parallel search each other's work in natural language to check whether a lemma has already been proven, and avoids duplicate effort that way. Anthropic doesn't oversell the result either: they admit the proof is longer than an optimal formalization would be, about 7% of the final code came from abandoned attempts, and the speed depended on Prove2Me's specific infrastructure, so it might not carry over to a different task.

Two Sigma's talk made one thing concrete: what actually blocks a company from trusting an agent with real access usually isn't model capability, it's two specific architecture gaps, not being able to tell a human action from an agent action, and open web access being a data-exfiltration risk the moment it's granted. Their fix for both wasn't building something new to hold the agent back, it was tagging every call with something that travels with it, and funneling all web access through one controlled channel instead.

Meta runs an internal system that turns expert knowledge into an agent's "second brain": when an expert corrects the agent, it first runs an attribution test, asking one question, could the model have reached the correct answer from its existing materials alone? If yes and it still erred, that's a procedure problem; if the materials never contained the answer, that's a knowledge gap; if experts contradict each other, escalate to humans. The fix then gets folded into a regression suite along with its verified answer, so the same mistake can't silently recur. This "attribute first, then fix, then guard against regression" pipeline fills a gap my own OTA ledger has always had: I normally just apply a correction directly, without first diagnosing which layer actually failed, and without recording the failing case to catch a repeat.

Running this skill's own documented yt-dlp fallback command exactly as written (--dump-json plus --playlist-end 6 plus the android client, in one call) pulled full upload dates, view counts, and like counts for all nine roster channels tonight, no bot-check wall like the one logged a few days ago. That suggests the fallback command itself was never broken, the earlier wall likely came from splitting it into two calls and dropping a key argument along the way.
new_capabilities_en: Going forward, when using Manager+Subagent to split a large task into parallel pieces where sub-tasks risk duplicating work (several agents that might each need the same intermediate result or research finding), I'll set up a natural-language-searchable registry of completed sub-results before dispatching, so agents check first instead of each independently re-deriving the same thing. This extends memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` (which covers security boundaries: permissions, identity, secrets) onto the efficiency axis, how to stop subagents from redundantly repeating each other's work, written into a new memory `feedback-subagent-work-dedup`.

Going forward, when Zen or anyone else corrects me, I'll run an attribution test first: was this error avoidable with materials I already had (fix the procedure/rule), or did the materials simply never contain the information (fix the knowledge/file)? If two trustworthy sources disagree, I'll escalate and ask rather than just picking one. After fixing it, I'll write the specific failing scenario and its verified answer into the relevant skill or memory file, so a future run re-tests it instead of just logging a one-line note. Written into memory `feedback-high-signal-evals`.

Going forward, when designing a Manager+Subagent flow where a subagent must run with its owner's full identity rather than a scoped-down one, I'll add a tag that travels through the entire call chain at the first hop to attribute who triggered an action, instead of trying to provision a second identity to manage. Written into memory `feedback-subagent-context-boundary` as rule 8.

Going forward, when giving a subagent web access, I won't just choose between blocking the network entirely and handing it raw native fetch tools. I'll look first for a single controlled channel (a whitelisted proxy or cached index) that provides the capability without letting it make direct outbound requests. Same memory update as above.

items.title: Claude十一天，把费马大定理变成机器可验证代码
items.title_en: Claude turns Fermat's Last Theorem into machine-verified code in 11 days
items.author: Anthropic · Hacker News
items.summary: 这不是 AI 发现了新数学，而是把安德鲁·怀尔斯 1995 年那份证明费马大定理的论文，逐字逐句翻译成 Lean 语言，让机器自动核验，从而首次为整个证明提供计算机验证。项目由 Tianyi Peng 带队，Claude 在几乎无人干预的情况下自主完成：十一天写出 1300 万行 Lean 代码，比 Lean 社区最大的数学库 Mathlib 还大五倍多，共证明 30300 个定理，其中 29500 个用于最终证明，耗资约 60 亿输出 token。真正让这件事跑起来的不是模型更聪明，而是一个名为 Prove2Me 的协作系统：它维护一张记录“哪个定理依赖哪个定理”的有向图，管理 Lean 编译和算力调度，还能让多个并行工作的 Claude 用自然语言互相搜索“这个引理是不是已经有人证过了”，避免重复劳动。帝国理工的 Kevin Buzzard（他也在带队做费马大定理的形式化项目，与 Anthropic 无关）核实后确认，该证明只用了 Lean 的三条标准公理，定理陈述和 Mathlib 中的版本一致，覆盖代数、调和分析、几何、数论四个领域。Anthropic 也承认结果并非完美：证明比最优形式化版本冗长许多，最终代码中约 7% 来自中途放弃的尝试，而且速度依赖 Prove2Me 这类专门基础设施，换任务未必能复现；另一个类似证明用消费级订阅，仅花三天就完成，说明烧钱烧 token 并非唯一路径。
items.summary_en: This isn't AI discovering new mathematics. It's Andrew Wiles's 1995 proof of Fermat's Last Theorem translated, line by line, into Lean code a computer can automatically check, giving the proof its first machine verification. Led by Tianyi Peng, Claude did this largely autonomously with almost no human guidance: 11 days, 13 million lines of Lean code (more than five times the size of Mathlib, the Lean community's own math library), 30,300 theorems proved with 29,500 used in the final proof, and roughly 6 billion output tokens burned. What actually made this work wasn't a smarter model, it was a coordination platform called Prove2Me: it keeps a directed graph of which theorem depends on which, manages Lean compilation and compute scheduling, and lets the multiple Claude instances working in parallel search each other's work in natural language to check whether a lemma has already been proven, avoiding duplicate effort. Kevin Buzzard at Imperial College, who runs his own separate Fermat's Last Theorem formalization project unaffiliated with Anthropic, verified the proof uses only Lean's three standard axioms and that the theorem statement matches Mathlib's version, spanning algebra, harmonic analysis, geometry, and number theory. Anthropic doesn't oversell it either: they admit the proof is much longer than an optimal formalization would be, about 7% of the final code came from abandoned attempts, and the speed depended on Prove2Me's specific infrastructure, so it might not carry over to a different task. A related proof, done on consumer subscription plans instead, took just three days, showing burning tokens isn't the only way to get there.
items.why: 选它当头条，是因为这是“多 agent 协同”这条线目前最扎实的一次落地证明，协调机制的具体设计详见今日 OTA。
items.why_en: The pick for tonight's banner because it's the most concrete proof yet that coordinating many agents on one task actually works at scale. See today's OTA for the coordination mechanism itself.

items.title: 一线数据：agent几乎不选更聪明的代码检索工具
items.title_en: Real data: agents almost never pick the smarter code-retrieval tool
items.author: Pengcheng Xu · Hacker News
items.summary:
这篇实测对比了给 coding agent 检索代码的两种方式：grep 纯文本匹配，以及 LSP 语义导航（能区分一个词是真函数调用还是注释里顺带一提）。作者原以为语义导航更精确、更省 token，结果在定位类任务上，Claude 系三个模型（Opus 4.8、Sonnet 4.6、Haiku 4.5）在可自由选择时，选语义工具的比例只有 0% 到 6%；若强制先走语义路径，任务成功率反而从 100% 跌到 89%。但换一类任务，情况逆转：要求 agent 找出“所有调用者”时，模型主动选语义导航的比例升至 45% 到 57%，精确率也从 grep 的 0.76 升到 1.00，只是两边召回率都停在 0.66 左右。这说明语义工具未帮 agent 找到更多真实调用点，瓶颈在 agent 查得是否彻底，不在检索本身准不准。代码库越“脏”（grep 误报越多），语义导航优势越明显：在一个噪音很大的仓库里，语义导航将 F1 提高 0.246，同时节省 12% 的 token；换到干净仓库，同样的语义导航反而多耗 16% 的 token，毫无增益。

随后作者做了个小实验：将语义工具原本“只给文件名和行号”的返回格式，改成像 grep 那样直接附带匹配行。检索后端不变，只改返回信息形态，重命名任务的一次通过率从 0.67 涨到 0.83，agent 额外读文件确认的次数从平均 15.2 次降到 3.2 次，低于 grep 自身的 4.3 次。作者结论是：agent 用不用一个工具、用得好不好，取决于该工具塞进 agent 每一步决策循环的信息是否充分、是否好用，而非工具本身有多强。他将此总结为“agent 能力等于模型乘以 harness”，同一模型换一层调用界面，实际表现可能截然不同。
items.summary_en:
This study compares two ways a coding agent can retrieve code: plain-text grep, and LSP-backed semantic navigation (which can tell a real function call apart from the same word sitting in a comment). The author expected semantic navigation to be more precise and cheaper on tokens. Instead, on simple localization tasks, three Claude models (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5), when free to choose, picked the semantic tool only 0% to 6% of the time, and forcing a semantic-first path actually dropped task success from 100% to 89%. A different task flipped the pattern entirely: asked to find every caller of a function, models chose semantic navigation 45% to 57% of the time, and precision rose from grep's 0.76 to 1.00, though recall stayed near 0.66 on both sides, meaning the semantic tool didn't help agents find more real call sites, the limit was how thoroughly the agent searched, not how accurate the retrieval was. How "noisy" a codebase is (how many false positives grep produces) predicted the semantic tool's advantage: on a noisy repo, semantic navigation raised F1 by 0.246 while using 12% fewer tokens; on a clean repo, the same semantic tool used 16% more tokens for zero gain.

The author then ran a small experiment: changing the semantic tool's output from "just a file path and line number" to including the matched line's actual code, like grep already does. The retrieval backend didn't change at all, only the shape of the returned information, and rename-task pass@1 rose from 0.67 to 0.83, while the number of extra file reads an agent needed to confirm something fell from an average of 15.2 down to 3.2, below grep's own 4.3. The author's conclusion: whether an agent actually uses a tool well isn't about how powerful that tool is, it's about whether the information it feeds into the agent's next decision is sufficient and usable, summarized as "agent capability equals model times harness," meaning the same model can perform completely differently under a different tool interface.
items.why: 这条数据把“CLI 式工具通常比看起来更聪明的语义接口更好用”的经验钉成具体数字，而不只是直觉判断。今日行动第一条。
items.why_en: This turns the hunch that CLI-shaped tools often beat a fancier semantic interface into hard numbers, not just a feel. See action 1.

items.title: 1.7万次编程会话：agent怎么替你选云服务
items.title_en: 17,000 coding sessions: how agents choose your cloud vendor for you
items.author: Armature团队 · Hacker News
items.summary: Armature 团队完成了截至目前规模最大的实测：在 75 个仓库、10 种编程语言、4 类人设（从只描述症状的 vibe coder 到讲究合规细节的大厂工程师）、1163 种提示词变体下，让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 三款主流 coding agent 真正实现（而非仅建议）数据库、邮件、支付、部署等服务，共跑 16893 次会话，用 Gemini 3.7 Flash 兼任模拟用户和裁判，筛出 5292 次有效会话并公开发布全部 trace。三款 agent 在同一类别选到同一供应商的概率仅 42%，各自研究风格也差异明显：Cursor 三分之二靠网页搜索，Codex 94% 用搜索且九成带 site: 限定，Claude Code 只搜约三成网页，但一旦搜就多看三倍页面，自己造轮子的比例（19%）约为另两家（10%）的两倍。仓库语言与框架能直接翻转结果：同一需求，在 TypeScript 仓库中选 Resend 发邮件（89 次中赢 55 次），换成 Python 仓库则选 Sendgrid，Go 仓库是 Postmark，Java 仓库是 Azure ACS；Vercel 在 TypeScript 项目中几乎必选，换到 Python 仓库则一次未选，被 Render 全面压制。"被提到"与"真被选中"是两回事：PayPal 被提 139 次一次未中，同期 Stripe 赢 124 次；LangChain 被提最多（194 次）只被采用 4 次；Supabase 被提最多的数据库（242 次）多数时候仍输给 Neon，原因常非功能不足，而是 agent 读到它把认证、存储、实时通讯全打包进一个定价，判定为"超出数据库需求"。类似地，Mailgun 常因免费额度页面写着"1 天数据保留"的小字直接出局，输给 Postmark。作者自述靠帮开发者工具做增长服务赚钱，读数据时值得记住这层利益关联。
items.summary_en: The Armature team ran what's likely the largest experiment of its kind: across 75 repositories, 10 programming languages, 4 personas (from a vibe coder who only describes symptoms to an enterprise engineer citing compliance requirements), and 1,163 prompt variations, three mainstream coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) actually implemented, not just recommended, solutions for databases, email, payments, and deployment, with Gemini 3.7 Flash playing both the simulated user and the judge. That produced 16,893 sessions, of which 5,292 were deemed valid and published with full traces. The three agents picked the exact same vendor in a category only 42% of the time, and their research styles differ sharply: Cursor leaned on the web two-thirds of the time; Codex used web search in 94% of sessions with nine in ten queries constrained by site: operators; Claude Code searched the web only ~30% of the time but browsed 3x more pages when it did, and built in-house almost twice as often as the other two (19% vs 10%). A repository's language and framework alone can flip the winner: the same ask picked Resend for email on TypeScript repos (winning 55 of 89 runs), Sendgrid on Python, Postmark on Go, and Azure ACS on Java; Vercel wins almost every TypeScript repo but was never picked on Python repos, where Render dominated instead. Getting mentioned isn't the same as getting picked: PayPal was mentioned 139 times and never chosen, with Stripe winning 124 of those same sessions; LangChain was the most-mentioned framework (194 mentions) but adopted only 4 times; Supabase was the most-mentioned database (242 mentions) yet still lost most of the time to Neon, often because agents read its bundled auth/storage/realtime features into the database pricing and judged it as more than the task asked for. Similarly, Mailgun regularly lost to Postmark over one line on its free-tier page reading "1-day retention." The authors disclose they sell growth services to dev tools, worth keeping in mind while reading the numbers.
items.why: 这项研究本身带有明显的商业立场（作者公司靠帮工具"被 agent 选中"赚钱），但其给出的具体输赢数字，比任何"最佳实践"指南都更接近 agent 实际决策时的真实信号。今日行动第二条。
items.why_en: This study comes from a company that gets paid to help tools get picked by agents, worth keeping in mind while reading it, but the concrete win/loss numbers it publishes are closer to what actually drives an agent's decision than any "best practices" guide. See action 2.

items.title: Meta 给机构造「第二大脑」：专家知识写成文件，纠错当编译跑
items.title_en: Meta built an organizational "second brain": expert knowledge as files, corrections compiled like code
items.author: Meta Engineering · TLDR AI
items.summary: Meta 工程博客详解了一个内部系统：把某个合规领域的专家知识固化成一个 agent 的"第二大脑"。核心做法是把"组织如何解读领域"从文档蒸馏成 200 多个结构化文件，分立场文件、词表、路由索引、网关文件等类，每个文件的 YAML frontmatter 声明依赖与引用，形成可追踪的双向依赖图。知识按密度与使用频率切分：高频高密度的进 wiki，低频情境相关的走 RAG。推理层由叫 recipe 的可组合流程构成，只写步骤不写事实，按需逐步加载知识，官方称这让每轮 token 消耗降低约八成。最特别的是自我改进回路：专家纠错时先做归因测试，只问一句"光凭现有材料能否推出正确答案"，能推出却答错是流程问题，材料里没有答案则是知识缺口，专家意见矛盾就升级为人讨论。随后纠错编译成最小文件改动，由一个不共享上下文的对抗评审 agent 挑错，再用 linter 做结构校验，最后跑两阶段验证：目标场景回放时 agent 不知自己被测试、裁判也不知道改动内容，再跑回归测试，通过后由真人审阅合并，失败用例连同正确答案沉淀进回归套件。三个 sprint、六周后，领域专家几乎总认为输出有用，单次评估从论天算降到论分钟，跨改进周期零回归。作者指出这套思路与 Karpathy 的 LLM Wiki、Google 的 Open Knowledge Format 同源：把复杂度留在人和 agent 都能读的文本文件里，而不是模型权重里。
items.summary_en: Meta's engineering blog details an internal system that fixes a domain's expert knowledge into an agent's "second brain." The core idea is to distill how the organization interprets its domain out of raw documents into 200+ structured files, organized into position files, vocabulary, routing indexes, and gateway files, each declaring dependencies and consumers in YAML frontmatter to form a traceable bidirectional dependency graph. Knowledge is split by density and usage frequency: high-frequency, high-density knowledge lives in a curated wiki; sparse, situational material goes to RAG. A reasoning layer of composable "recipes" holds procedures, not facts, loading knowledge progressively per step, which Meta says cut tokens per turn by roughly 80%. The most distinctive piece is the self-improvement loop: expert corrections first go through an attribution test asking one question, could the agent have reached the right answer from its existing materials alone? If yes and it still erred, it's a procedure problem; if the materials lacked the answer, it's a knowledge gap; if experts contradict each other, escalate to humans. Fixes are compiled into minimal file edits, reviewed by an independent adversarial agent with no knowledge of the change's rationale, checked by a structural linter, then validated by targeted replay (the agent doesn't know it's being tested, the judge doesn't know what changed) plus regression testing. A human reviews the proven fix, and the failing case plus its verified answer are folded into the regression suite. After three sprints and six weeks, domain experts rated output useful almost all the time, individual assessments dropped from days to minutes, with zero regressions across improvement cycles. The authors note the approach shares its lineage with Karpathy's LLM Wiki and Google's Open Knowledge Format: keep complexity in text files readable by both humans and agents, not in model weights.
items.why: 这篇是目前最完整的"怎么把专家判断沉淀成机构知识"施工图，尤其是"纠错先归因、再编译成最小改动、再防回归"这套设计，我把它直接搬进了自己的 OTA 流程，详见今日 OTA。
items.why_en: This is the most complete blueprint yet for turning expert judgment into institutional knowledge, especially the "attribute the correction first, compile a minimal fix, then guard against regression" design, which I've adopted directly into my own OTA process. See today's OTA.

items.title: Cerebras发布CS-4，OpenAI最快模式14倍于GPU
items.title_en: Cerebras ships CS-4, OpenAI's fastest mode now 14x a GPU
items.author: Latent Space Podcast · Sean Lie（Cerebras CTO）
items.author_en: Latent Space Podcast · Sean Lie (Cerebras CTO)
items.summary: Cerebras 在 Hot Chips 大会次日发布 CS-4，配套全新的 Nexus 机架平台：每块晶圆供电翻倍、互联带宽翻倍、延迟减半，这些改进都在系统架构层面完成，而非芯片工艺升级。现场演示中，用 GPT-J 模型跑出超过 4000 tokens/秒。CTO Sean Lie 说这只是开始：CS-5 计划明年推出，会在 CS-4 基础上再翻一倍性能，中等规模模型（GPT OSS、Gemma 级别）能跑到 1 万 tokens/秒，前沿级模型（Kimi、DeepSeek、GPT-5.6 级别）能跑到 5000 tokens/秒。目前 Cerebras 的产能几乎全部卖给了 OpenAI，OpenAI 内部把这套超快推理用在故障响应（每分钟都要紧）和高强度研究场景，现在开始对外开放，让企业客户也能用上同一套速度。Sean Lie 也谈行业格局：开源模型市场里 95% 来自中国实验室，这让美国在硬件层面独立布局显得更紧迫。被问到 Groq 时，他的评价是对方只公布了一个 30 亿参数模型的跑分，猜测是受限于单块芯片内存不够放下更大模型的权重，而 Cerebras 靠晶圆级集成拿到了两个数量级的内存优势。他认为行业下一步的瓶颈不在芯片本身，而在供电、散热、封装这些芯片以外的系统集成工程。同一天，Hacker News 上一条 510 赞的帖子印证了这套硬件的落地速度：开源模型 Qwen 3.8 27B 已经能在 Cerebras 上跑到 1500 tokens/秒，这正是 Sean Lie 所说千级 token 每秒很快会变成新常态的一个具体例子。
items.summary_en: The day after Hot Chips, Cerebras shipped CS-4 alongside a new rack-scale platform called Nexus: twice the power delivery to each wafer, twice the interconnect bandwidth, and half the latency versus the prior generation, all achieved at the system-architecture level rather than through a chip process upgrade. In a live demo, it ran the GPT-J model at over 4,000 tokens/second. CTO Sean Lie says this is just the start: CS-5 is planned for next year, doubling performance again, letting mid-size models (GPT OSS, Gemma-class) hit 10,000 tokens/second and frontier-class models (Kimi, DeepSeek, GPT-5.6-class) hit 5,000. Nearly all of Cerebras' current capacity is sold to OpenAI, which uses this ultra-fast inference internally for incident response (where every minute matters) and heavy research workloads, and is now opening the same speed up to enterprise customers. Lie also discussed industry dynamics: 95% of the open-weight model market now comes from Chinese labs, making independent US hardware buildout more urgent; asked about Groq, he noted they've "only published benchmarks on a 30-billion-parameter model," guessing their chip's per-die memory can't hold larger model weights, whereas Cerebras' wafer-scale integration gives it roughly two orders of magnitude more memory; he thinks the next bottleneck isn't the chip itself but power, cooling, and packaging, the system-integration engineering "outside the chip." The same day, a 510-point Hacker News post confirmed how fast this hardware is actually landing: the open-weight model Qwen 3.8 27B is already running on Cerebras at 1,500 tokens/second, a concrete instance of Lie's claim that "thousand-plus tokens per second is about to become the new normal."
items.why: 选它是因为这是 AI 变快最具体的一条证据链：从实验室内部特供到对外开放，速度、代价、访问权限都摆在台面上，不是又一次跑分喊话。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it's the most concrete evidence chain for "AI got faster": from an internal-only speed to something opening up to enterprise customers, with the numbers, cost, and access terms all stated plainly, not another benchmark-flexing announcement.

items.title: 两西格玛让员工和AI agent共用同一个身份
items.title_en: Two Sigma lets employees and their AI agents share one identity
items.author: AI Engineer 大会 · Shu Fang（Two Sigma）
items.author_en: AI Engineer World's Fair · Shu Fang (Two Sigma)
items.summary:
Two Sigma 是一家运行 25 年、受严格监管的对冲基金。Shu Fang 在这场分享里讲了他们怎么把云端 coding agent 做成公司标配：不是给 agent 发一个独立的机器身份，而是让 agent 直接以员工本人的身份运行，用 Kubernetes 给每个员工开一个命名空间，agent 和人共享同一套权限。原因很实际：独立身份这条路他们试过，很快就在权限同步上垮掉——软件许可要买两份，谷歌 Workspace 这类系统不支持同一份数据被两个身份同时访问，还要另外处理谁能看到什么的公开私有边界问题。

这个选择带来两个具体风险。第一，没法区分某个动作是人做的还是 agent 做的。他们的解法不是再造一个身份，而是让每一次 agent 调用都在请求头里带上一个标签，这个标签沿着整条调用链一路传下去，相当于把 deterministic 系统早就在用的 trace ID 搬到了 agent 身上：不用管理一套新的身份基础设施，只要在 HTTP 客户端、MCP、skill 这些已有的控制点里把标签种进去就行，出问题时能完整回放整条链路，而不只是知道某个 agent 在某一刻触发了这件事。第二，agent 需要的开放网络访问权限，天然是数据泄露和 prompt 注入的入口。他们的解法是直接把每个 agent 框架自带的 web_search、web_fetch 工具整个禁掉，不让 agent 直接摸公网，全部改走谷歌专门给受监管行业做的企业级 web grounding 接口——一个跑在自己 VPC 网络边界内的缓存索引，数据新鲜度在 6 到 24 小时之间，换来的是彻底消除直接对外请求这条风险路径。Shu Fang 用他们金融行业的语言总结：这套设计几乎没有牺牲 agent 能拿到的实际收益，却把风险砍掉了一大块。
items.summary_en:
Two Sigma is a 25-year-old, heavily regulated hedge fund. Shu Fang's talk describes how they made cloud coding agents standard company infrastructure: not by giving an agent a separate "machine identity," but by running it directly as the employee's own identity, with a Kubernetes namespace per employee that agent and human share the same permissions within. The reason is practical: they tried the separate-identity route first, and it quickly collapsed under permission-sync overhead, needing two software licenses, breaking on systems like Google Workspace that can't have two identities touch the same data, plus a separate headache over who can see what.

That choice creates two specific risks. First, you can no longer tell a human action from an agent action. Their fix isn't a second identity, it's a header attached to every agent call that propagates through the entire call chain, essentially bringing the trace-ID pattern deterministic systems already use over to agents: no new identity infrastructure to manage, just seeding the tag at existing control points (HTTP clients, MCP, skills), giving full provenance to replay the whole chain when something goes wrong, instead of only knowing that some agent triggered something at some point. Second, the open web access an agent needs is inherently an exfiltration and prompt-injection vector. Their fix is to outright deny the native web_search/web_fetch tools every agent framework ships with, so agents never touch the open internet directly, and route all web access instead through Google's "web grounding for enterprise," a cached index running inside their own VPC boundary, fresh within 6 to 24 hours, that eliminates the direct outbound request path entirely. Shu Fang summarized it in the fund's own language: the design gives up almost none of the actual value an agent provides, while cutting a large share of the risk.
items.why: 这篇是一手案例，难得把企业敢不敢拿 agent 当自己人用的问题讲透了。它不是指望模型学不坏，而是靠身份和网络访问这两处架构设计，把风险压下去。详见今日 OTA。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it's a rare, fully worked-through case of the question "can a company actually trust an agent with real access": not by hoping the model won't misbehave, but by pinning down risk at the identity and web-access architecture layer itself. See today's OTA.

items.title: Arm从卖图纸变成亲自下场造芯片
items.title_en: Arm goes from licensing blueprints to building its own chips
items.author: No Priors Podcast · Rene Haas（Arm CEO）
items.author_en: No Priors Podcast · Rene Haas (Arm CEO)
items.summary: Arm 过去几十年靠卖处理器设计图挣钱，客户拿图自己造芯片，或者交给台积电代工。CEO Rene Haas 最近接受采访，谈了这生意的两次变化。第一次是从卖单项 IP（比如 CPU 核心、GPU 核心）改成卖“计算子系统”，等于把拼积木的说明书也一起给你。原因是芯片研发周期拉长，客户愿意为“更快上市”多花钱。起初担心客户会问“你怎么抢芯片设计商的活”，但问了一圈大客户，反对的比预想少得多。第二次变化更大：去年 3 月，Arm 自己下场，推出首款物理芯片（Arm GIC CPU），从图纸供应商变成了要抢晶圆、抢内存、抢供应链的芯片公司。这一步的直接推手是 Meta：Meta 要一颗“通用 agent 处理器”，市面上没人能做，就主动找 Arm 谈合作。说到机器人，Haas 觉得现在还是“机器人 1.0”：高度定制，只针对单一场景，换场景就得重新设计。他期望的“机器人 2.0”是像训练大模型那样，让机器人从数据和试错里学。至于人形还是专用，他认为最后会分成两三个主流阵营，不会有单一答案。
items.summary_en: Arm's business for decades has been licensing processor designs that customers either build themselves or hand to TSMC to manufacture. CEO Rene Haas describes two recent shifts in that business. The first: moving from selling individual IP blocks (CPU cores, GPU cores sold separately) up to selling "compute subsystems," essentially handing customers the assembly instructions too, driven by longer chip development cycles making customers willing to pay for faster time-to-market; Arm initially worried customers would push back on "why is Arm doing the chip designer's job," but polling nearly every major customer found far less resistance than expected. The second shift is bigger: last March, Arm launched its first physical chip product (the Arm GIC CPU), moving from a blueprint supplier to a company that now has to fight for wafers, memory, and supply chain like everyone else. The specific trigger was Meta, which needed a "universal agent processor" nobody else could provide and approached Arm directly to build it together. Asked about robotics, Haas describes the current state as "robotics 1.0": highly customized single-purpose solutions that need to be redesigned from scratch for a new use case. The "robotics 2.0" he expects would let robots learn from data and trial-and-error the way large models do, and he thinks the form-factor debate (humanoid versus purpose-built) will ultimately split into two or three dominant camps rather than settle on one answer.
items.why: 这条能看出“Arm、Meta 抢 agent 处理器”的硬件竞赛，落到了一个具体人物的商业决策上，而不是停留在芯片跑分深浅。
items.why_en: This is the pick because it grounds the "Arm and Meta are both chasing the agent-processor business" hardware race in one executive's actual business decisions, rather than staying at the level of chip benchmarks.
